home.heroEyebrow: 墨 SUMI · BUILT ON SUMINANET 黒
home.heroSub: Sumina reads the cursive kuzushiji in your scans of woodblock prints and manuscripts, lets you correct the draft, and renders centuries of Japanese into English you can actually read.

how_steps.title: Upload a scan
how_steps.body: Drop in a photograph or scan of any woodblock print or handwritten manuscript — modern or Edo-era.

how_steps.title: Transcribe & correct
how_steps.body: SuminaNet detects each cursive character and proposes a reading. You review the results and correct anything it missclassified.

how_steps.title: Translate
how_steps.body: Get fluent English alongside the original, drawn straight from the corrected transcription.

about.title: Why Sumina exists
about.creditLine: 墨奈 Sumina — 幸 by Amina Felic.

p1.text: Most people — even fluent readers of modern Japanese — cannot read

, the flowing cursive in which nearly every Edo-period book, letter, and ledger was written. Centuries of literature, science, and ordinary life sit locked behind a hand almost no one is trained to decipher.

p2.text: , an in-house character-recognition model inspired by KuroNet — the pioneering system built by Tarin Clanuwat and collaborators — with a human correction step and translation, so a scan becomes a reading, and a reading becomes English. Made for researchers, students, and anyone curious enough to look closely.

p3.text: Sumina is a research prototype, not a commercial product. It is free to use, and we do not collect personal information. Please see our
for details. The model was trained using data from CODH. Translation is performed using the Mecab and Unidic for normalization and the Claude API (Somnet model) for translation.

acknowledgments.text: Sumina began as a thesis project at Goethe University Frankfurt, supervised by
and his lab, with generous guidance on the historical Japanese side from
. Their support made this project possible.

policy.title: Privacy Policy
policy.intro: Sumina is a research prototype for transcribing and translating Kuzushiji (cursive historical Japanese) manuscripts. This page explains what happens to the images and text you submit.
policy.collectIntro: Using Sumina involves the following data:
collectItems: Uploaded images — processed in server memory to detect and transcribe characters, then discarded once your request completes. Images are not saved to disk or retained after processing.
Transcribed text — if you request a translation, the transcribed text (including any corrections you make) is sent to our translation provider to generate the result.
IP address — held briefly in server memory to enforce per-IP rate limits, then cleared automatically; never written to disk or kept after the server restarts.
Language preference — your choice of English or German is saved in your browser's local storage only, and is never sent to our servers.
policy.useIntro: The data above is used solely to:
useItems: Run the transcription and translation you request
Prevent abuse of the service through rate limiting
policy.thirdPartyText: Translation is powered by Anthropic's Claude model, accessed via the OpenRouter API. When you request a translation, the transcribed text you submit is sent to this third-party provider to generate the translation. No images are shared with this provider — only text.
policy.protectionText: We do not create user accounts and do not collect names, email addresses, or other personal identifiers. Uploaded images are never stored beyond the lifetime of your request.

detailedSections.heading: Responsible party
paragraphs: Amina Felic, Goethe Universität, Bockenheimer Landstraße 133, Frankfurt am Main, Deutschland.
This privacy policy explains which personal data we process, for what purposes, and to what extent as part of providing the Sumina application.

detailedSections.heading: Overview of processing
paragraphs: We process uploaded images to detect and transcribe manuscript characters and to generate translations. The images are processed only in server memory for the duration of the request and are not stored on disk.
We process transcribed text when a translation is requested. The text may be sent to a translation provider to generate the output. We do not share images with that provider.
We process IP addresses temporarily to enforce rate limits. The values are held only in memory and are cleared automatically.
We process the user choice of language only in the browser's local storage and never send it to our servers.

detailedSections.heading: Legal basis and purpose
paragraphs: The processing is based on our legitimate interest in operating and securing the application and on the contract between the user and the service provider for the requested transcription and translation functionality.
The purposes are to provide the requested service, prevent misuse and abuse, and ensure technical reliability of the application.

detailedSections.heading: Security measures
paragraphs: We use technical and organizational safeguards proportionate to the risk, including access controls, encrypted HTTPS connections, and short-lived in-memory processing. We do not keep user accounts, personal profiles, or persistent image storage.
We do not collect names, email addresses, or other identifying personal data as part of the standard transcription process.

detailedSections.heading: Data retention and deletion
paragraphs: We delete personal data as soon as the underlying processing purpose no longer applies and no legal retention obligation prevents deletion. Uploaded images and submitted text are processed only in server memory for the duration of the request and discarded afterward — nothing is written to disk.
IP addresses are held only briefly in memory to enforce rate limits and are cleared automatically. They are not written to log files on disk.

detailedSections.heading: Hosting provider
paragraphs: To provide this service, we use storage space and computing capacity rented from a server provider (web host). Legal basis: legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

Provider: 1&1 IONOS SE, Elgendorfer Str. 57, 56410 Montabaur, Germany. Website: https://www.ionos.de. Privacy policy: https://www.ionos.de/terms-gtc/terms-privacy. Data processing agreement (AVV): https://www.ionos.de/hilfe/datenschutz/allgemeine-informationen-zur-datenschutz-grundverordnung-dsgvo/vereinbarung-zur-auftragsverarbeitung-avv-mit-ionos-abschliessen/.

detailedSections.heading: Translation service provider
paragraphs: To generate the translation, the transcribed text you've corrected (never images) is sent to Anthropic's Claude model, accessed via the OpenRouter API. Legal basis: performance of the contract to provide the translation feature you requested (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).

Providers: Anthropic PBC (San Francisco, USA) and OpenRouter, Inc. (USA). Because both providers are located outside the EU/EEA, this involves a transfer of data to a third country. For details on their respective safeguards, see their privacy policies: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy and https://openrouter.ai/privacy. We recommend verifying the current state of these before this goes live in real public production, as provider policies can change.

detailedSections.heading: Rights of data subjects
paragraphs: If you submit data to the service, you may request confirmation of processing, access to your data, correction, deletion, or restriction of processing in accordance with the applicable data protection law.
If you believe your rights have been violated, you may also contact the relevant data protection authority.
